review_scope: Read all 90 records; judged every same-split candidate in all six domains for the 45 technology/science/qa queries. All candidates omitted from positive_grades are reviewed grade 0. Reviewed BN/BL passages and query variants against EN; source grounding checked against pinned NIST, NASA and USGS files. Agent audit only.

issues.issue: Mixed-script typo shamলabe contains Bengali ল inside the romanized Banglish query.
issues.suggestion: Use shamlabe or shamলabe corrected entirely to Latin: shamlabe.
issues.resolution_review: q_bl now uses entirely Latin shamlabe; PaaS meaning preserved.

issues.issue: Variant asks what follows the red giant stage, whereas main queries ask for all end-of-life stages. It presupposes one answer stage and narrows the request.
issues.suggestion: surjo jiboner shesh dike kon kon stage diye jabe?
issues.resolution_review: Variant now asks for all late-life stages, matching the primary question.

issues.issue: noshto hote pare asks which systems may be damaged/ruined, stronger than disruption or bighno in the main queries.
issues.suggestion: earth er dike cme ele kon system e bighno hote pare?
issues.resolution_review: Variant now asks about bighno (disruption), preserving main-query strength.

issues.issue: Variant asks why ash and SO2 climate effects differ in general, losing the main query's specifically shorter-lasting effect.
issues.suggestion: volcano ash er climate effect sulfur dioxide er cheye kom din thake keno?
issues.resolution_review: Variant now explicitly asks about shorter-lasting climate effects.

issues.issue: Variant supplies sunlight reflection, the key mechanism that the main query asks the retriever to find. This changes retrieval difficulty.
issues.suggestion: volcano er sulfate aerosol nicher atmosphere thanda kore kivabe?
issues.resolution_review: Variant asks for cooling mechanism without supplying reflection.

issues.issue: The second sentence renders the source's mandatory federal use requirement as told to use (ব্যবহার করতে বলা হয়েছে / use korte bola hoy), weakening explicit requires in EN and SHALL in pinned NIST block 108.
issues.suggestion: Use explicit বাধ্যতামূলক / use korte hoy wording.
issues.resolution_review: BN now says বাধ্যতামূলক and BL use korte hoy, preserving mandatory federal use.

issues.issue: কার্বন নিঃসরণ omits ডাইঅক্সাইড, while EN/BL specify CO2; carbon emissions is common shorthand but broadens the literal query.
issues.resolution_review: BN query now explicitly specifies কার্বন ডাইঅক্সাইড.

technology-01.rationale: technology-01 identifies automatic provisioning without staff. technology-08 mentions provisioning storage but says nothing about avoiding provider interaction; technology-04 concerns demand scaling, not self-service.

technology-02.rationale: technology-02 explicitly identifies broad network access across phones, tablets, laptops and workstations. technology-06 offers applications but does not specify heterogeneous device access.

technology-03.rationale: technology-03 explains shared physical/virtual resources, multiple consumers and demand reassignment. technology-09 describes organization eligibility, not pooling mechanics.

technology-04.rationale: technology-04 identifies rapid expansion and contraction with demand. technology-03 reallocates pooled resources but does not identify capacity elasticity or sudden scale changes.

technology-05.rationale: technology-05 identifies resource metering, monitoring and reports. technology-03 allocates resources but supplies no consumption accounting.

technology-06.rationale: technology-06 names SaaS and provider applications without OS management. technology-07 also removes OS management but deploys the consumer application, so does not answer the requested provider-app model.

technology-07.rationale: technology-07 names PaaS for own-app deployment without managing the OS. technology-06 uses provider applications; technology-08 grants OS control. Neither meets the requested combination.

technology-08.rationale: technology-08 explicitly assigns OS control to IaaS customers. technology-06 and technology-07 explicitly withhold it, so neither answers which model gives control.

technology-09.rationale: technology-09 supplies both private and community customer groups. technology-10 names these deployment types but never defines their audiences.

technology-10.rationale: technology-10 contrasts public access with combined distinct infrastructures and portability. technology-09 defines private/community audiences but no hybrid arrangement.

technology-11.rationale: technology-11 directly permits single-factor AAL1. technology-13 concerns AAL2 and cannot answer AAL1 requirements.

technology-12.rationale: technology-12 defines elapsed-since-authentication and inactivity timeouts. Other test documents do not address session expiration.

technology-13.rationale: technology-13 directly requires two distinct AAL2 factors. technology-14 describes biometric plus physical authentication without specifying AAL2 requirements; technology-15 addresses phishing resistance, not factor count.

technology-14.rationale: technology-14 explicitly rejects standalone biometrics and requires a physical authenticator. technology-13 requires two AAL2 factors but does not establish biometrics cannot be standalone authenticators.

technology-15.rationale: technology-15 requires at least one phishing-resistant AAL2 option. technology-13 gives factor count, which does not answer phishing-resistance availability.

science-01.rationale: science-01 explains the nonsolid plasma and different equatorial/polar periods. science-02 partially supplies the nonsolid premise, without rotation rates. science-09 is galactic revolution rather than differential rotation.

science-02.rationale: science-02 explicitly identifies the photosphere as emitting most visible sunlight. science-03 locates energy-generating fusion in the core but does not identify the layer emitting the visible light.

science-03.rationale: science-03 identifies hydrogen-to-helium fusion in the core. science-02 describes emitted visible light without its powering reaction.

science-04.rationale: science-04 names the corona and its greater temperature than the photosphere. science-03 gives a hotter core but that is not an outer region.

science-05.rationale: science-05 answers both the no-holes misconception and cooler appearance. science-02 identifies the photosphere but does not explain sunspots.

science-06.rationale: science-06 gives release of magnetic energy as the flare trigger and contrasts CMEs. science-07 describes CME clouds and damage but never gives a solar-flare trigger.

science-07.rationale: science-07 names satellites and power grids. science-06 describes flares/CMEs but no disrupted Earth systems.

science-08.rationale: science-08 names and defines the heliosphere. science-04 describes the corona rather than the large bubble beyond planets.

science-09.rationale: science-09 provides approximately 230 million years for galactic orbit. science-01 gives solar spin periods, not galactic travel time.

science-10.rationale: science-10 gives red giant then white dwarf. No other same-split passage supplies stellar end-of-life stages; science-09 only supplies orbital motion.

science-11.rationale: science-11 links tilt to different direct illumination while orbiting, explaining opposing seasons. science-14 gives atmospheric composition/protection, not seasonal geometry.

science-12.rationale: science-12 explicitly contrasts solid inner and liquid outer cores. science-13 discusses moving lithospheric plates, not core states.

science-13.rationale: science-13 lists sliding, overriding, collision and separation. science-12 locates mantle/crust but gives no plate motion causing earthquakes.

science-14.rationale: science-14 gives nitrogen at 78%, above oxygen and other gases. qa-15 discusses CO2 emissions, not atmospheric abundance.

science-15.rationale: science-15 explains trapped charged particles colliding with molecules and making them glow. science-14 describes atmospheric gases and radiation protection, not aurora creation. science-07 is in the other split and is excluded.

qa-01.rationale: qa-01 covers atmosphere, surface and underground. qa-02 partially identifies aquifer groundwater storage. qa-03 partially locates groundwater and surface rivers/ocean in a return pathway. qa-05 partially identifies land, ocean and atmosphere water reservoirs through exchange, without underground. qa-06 partially identifies rivers, lakes, reservoirs and aquifers as water sources. qa-10 says storage matters but does not locate any stores.

qa-02.rationale: qa-02 explicitly locates aquifer groundwater in rock cracks and pores. qa-01 says underground but not rock spaces; qa-03 says infiltration/recharge but not aquifer pore occupancy.

qa-03.rationale: qa-03 names springs and discharge into rivers/ocean. qa-01 states movement between stores without explaining how groundwater emerges; qa-06 withdraws groundwater by people rather than natural return.

qa-04.rationale: qa-04 assigns evaporation to solar energy and downhill flow/precipitation to gravity. qa-05 names up/down processes but does not attribute either to sunlight or gravity.

qa-05.rationale: qa-05 directly names evapotranspiration and precipitation. qa-04 independently answers the broad up/down-process question with evaporation into vapor and falling rain/snow/hail. qa-01 merely mentions movement among stores without the mechanisms.

qa-06.rationale: qa-06 directly says dams and drainage change storage and movement. qa-01 notes water stores but does not connect changes to dams or draining wetlands.

qa-07.rationale: qa-07 explicitly names rainfall/irrigation washing fertilizers and pesticides into rivers/groundwater. qa-03 describes groundwater recharge but does not establish transport of farm chemicals.

qa-08.rationale: qa-08 gives altered precipitation patterns and flood/drought frequency, intensity and duration. qa-09 addresses quality, not timing/extremes; qa-10 defines timing without climate effects.

qa-09.rationale: qa-09 gives marine shell/skeleton damage and soot/ash contamination. qa-07 gives other pollution routes but not acidification or wildfire.

qa-10.rationale: qa-10 explicitly requires quantity, timing and quality. qa-07 partially explains why quantity is insufficient by identifying chemical/sewage contamination. qa-08 partially explains variable timing and extremes; qa-09 partially explains quality loss through acidity and wildfire pollutants. qa-01 describes stores and movement but does not give a usable-supply limitation.

qa-11.rationale: qa-11 directly contrasts rapid ash fallout with SO2-derived cooling aerosol. qa-12 partially explains the SO2 aerosol cooling side, without ash or residence time. qa-13 partially documents three-year cooling after SO2 injection, without ash comparison. qa-14 compares eruption emissions and regional cooling but provides no persistence explanation.

qa-12.rationale: qa-12 explains reflection of sunlight back to space. qa-11 only states that SO2 can form cooling aerosols, without explaining how they cool; qa-13 gives an observed effect, not its radiative mechanism.

qa-13.rationale: qa-13 explicitly gives three years. qa-14 mentions similar regional cooling but no duration; qa-11 gives ash fallout time, not Pinatubo cooling duration.

qa-14.rationale: qa-14 directly gives Laki 120 million versus Pinatubo 20 million tons. qa-13 partially supplies the Pinatubo comparison value but cannot select the larger eruption alone. qa-11 and qa-12 contain no eruption-specific quantities.

qa-15.rationale: qa-15 explicitly gives historical human/volcanic CO2 totals and 80–270 ratio. qa-14 compares SO2 from two volcanoes, not human versus volcanic CO2.

recheck.summary: Re-read corrected issue-bearing records and corrected banking/business/conversation text. All seven issues in this review are resolved. Reviewer-a corrections preserve meaning and do not introduce relevant cross-domain candidates for the technology/science/qa query scope. All 45 positive_grades mappings and their same-split zero judgments remain valid. No material was edited by this reviewer.
